subject: Cerulean Health — VPC data handling, residency & deletion Q&A
messages:
From: Linda Kramer <linda.kramer@ceruleanhealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: devops@ceruleanhealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: VPC deployment — data residency, retention, deletion Qs

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we evaluate Redwood Private for our regulated workloads, our legal and platform teams surfaced a few specific questions about how data is handled inside a VPC deployment. Can you confirm the following?

1) Where are inference request payloads and generated outputs stored by default in a Private (VPC) deployment? Is there an option to point Redwood at our S3-compatible bucket (customer-controlled storage)?
2) What are the default retention guarantees for request logs, model KV cache, and persistent artifacts (model files, snapshots)? Can we set/limit retention to specific values per dataset/route?
3) If Cerulean issues a deletion request, describe the end-to-end deletion process and expected timelines. Can Redwood provide an attestation or audit entry once deletion completes?
4) How are encryption keys handled — can we use our own KMS/HSM (customer-managed keys)?
5) Do backups or snapshots ever replicate outside the customer’s chosen region, including for support/debugging?

We also need language we can share with procurement for a deletion SLA and evidence types (audit logs, object-store purge receipts).

Appreciate a short Q&A and any templates you can provide.

Best,
Linda Kramer
Head of Legal
Cerulean Health


From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Kramer <linda.kramer@ceruleanhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: VPC deployment — data residency, retention, deletion Qs

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (security & privacy) who can add the technical detail and any standard attestation artifacts we provide. Below is a concise summary; Marissa will expand on the implementation specifics and timelines.

Quick answers up front:
- Storage/residency: For Redwood Private (VPC) we support customer-controlled object stores. You can configure Redwood to use an S3-compatible bucket that you own and control in your cloud account/region; artifacts and persistent logs will be written there by default when configured.
- Retention controls: We offer per-route and per-bucket retention policies. Default logs retention is 90 days, but you can set 30/90/365 or custom values for specific datasets. KV caches are ephemeral by design but may be written to a customer bucket for warm-starts if you enable persistence.
- Deletion flow & timeline: Deletion is an API-driven workflow: (1) customer initiates delete (API/console/DocuSign-backed request), (2) system flags and begins async purge of objects and metadata, (3) background job purges snapshots and bucket objects, (4) system emits audit records and a deletion attestation PDF. Typical completion window for object-store purge is 24–72 hours depending on object count; snapshots may take up to 7 days to fully expire from all layers.
- Keys: We support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM integrations in our Private deployments; envelope encryption is used so raw data keys are under your control when configured.
- Backups/replication: By default backups remain in-region and in your account/bucket when you use customer-controlled storage. Redwood does not replicate persistent customer data outside the configured region unless you explicitly enable cross-region disaster recovery.

Attachments: I’ve attached our SOC2 summary and a VPC deployment checklist that includes the storage/KMS integration steps. Marissa — could you add the technical deletion sequence and suggested SLA wording (we heard "deletion attestation" and "audit receipts" as requested)?

If helpful we can do a short call with Cerulean DevOps and Legal this week to walk through the checklist and finalize wording for procurement.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Kramer <linda.kramer@ceruleanhealth.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: devops@ceruleanhealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: VPC deployment — data residency, retention, deletion Qs

Hi Linda — thanks for the questions. I’ve outlined the technical behavior below and included example SLA language you can give to procurement.

Technical details (Private / VPC deployment):
- Data plane placement: When configured in "customer-controlled storage" mode, all persistent artifacts that Redwood would normally write (model bundles, route-level logs, persistent KV warm-start files, debug bundles) are written directly to an object store you provide (S3/GCS/Azure Blob via IAM role or service principal). The Redwood control plane (hosted in our control-account if you opt in) stores only metadata and routing info; sensitive artifacts remain in your account.
- In-memory & ephemeral caches: GPU memory and ephemeral KV caches exist only on the host for runtime and are not persisted unless you explicitly enable KV persistence to your bucket.
- Deletion workflow (detailed):
  1) Request: Deletion initiated via API/console or as a signed DocuSign request (we attach the signed doc to the audit record).
  2) Quarantine flag: Objects and associated metadata are marked for purge (non-discoverable via API).
  3) Background purge: An idempotent background process issues object delete calls to your bucket and removes related database entries. For large object sets we do a batched delete; delete job status is exposed via the API.
  4) Snapshots & backups: Scheduled snapshots are also queued for removal; for cloud-native object stores these are removed from the same region. If you use cross-region replication, you must disable replication or request explicit coordination for remote-region purges.
  5) Attestation: Upon completion the system emits a signed deletion attestation containing: list of purged object prefixes, timestamps, job IDs, and a checksum of the audit log.

Timelines (typical):
- Small deletes (<10k objects): 24 hours
- Medium (10k–1M objects): 48–72 hours
- Large (>1M objects or multi-snapshot): up to 7 days (we provide progress updates and final attestation)

Encryption & keys:
- Customer-managed KMS: Supported. When enabled, object metadata and secrets use envelope encryption; master keys remain in your KMS. We never persist plaintext data keys outside the VPC where configured.

Backups/Support access:
- Support access to customer data is disabled by default. If you opt to enable limited support access for debugging, that access is audited and requires an approval workflow (and you can scope it to a specific timeframe). Backups/snapshots remain in-region unless you explicitly enable out-of-region replication.

Suggested procurement language (deletion SLA excerpt):
"Redwood Inference will, upon receipt of a written deletion request from Cerulean Health, commence a purge of customer data stored in the customer-configured object store. Redwood will complete deletion of objects and associated persistent artifacts within 7 days for standard workloads and provide a signed deletion attestation within 72 hours of job completion. For large data volumes parties will coordinate project timelines in good faith."

Evidence types provided: signed deletion attestation (PDF), audit log export (JSON), object-store delete job IDs and scan report, DocuSign request copy.

Action items:
- Rishi: share the attestation template and the procurement-friendly SLA snippet.
- Linda / DevOps: confirm whether you will use customer-managed KMS and whether cross-region replication is enabled on your side.

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync with DevOps to walk through the lifecycle and demonstrate the attestation flow.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Linda / team — quick note from my side. We reviewed Marissa’s proposed deletion SLA language and the attestation artifacts we can provide. For Cerulean (deal RDW-5231) we can commit to the following contract language in the SOW/addendum: 

- Standard deletion target: completion within 7 days for full purges, with progress updates for large volumes.
- Attestation: signed deletion attestation (PDF) + audit log export will be provided within 72 hours of job completion.
- Optional upgrade: Cerulean may opt into a 30-day guaranteed purge window with priority processing and same-day start for deletes under 500k objects (additional fee applies).

Rishi — please initiate the DocuSign addendum referencing the deletion attestation template I’ve attached and include the procurement SLA line. Linda — once you confirm KMS choice and whether cross-region replication is turned on we’ll finalize the SOW language.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
